**Observations:**
- Microscopy image at 100µm scale
- Branched conidiophores with clusters of oval/elliptical conidia at the tips
- Conidia arranged in grape-like (botryose) clusters — the hallmark of *Botrytis cinerea*
- Multiple branching points visible, consistent with Botrytis conidiophore morphology

**Reasoning:**
The branched conidiophores bearing dense, grape-like clusters of oval conidia at their tips is the classic microscopic signature of *Botrytis cinerea*, the causal agent of Gray Mold. No other class in the list produces this distinctive microscopic morphology. Powdery Mildew has chasmothecia/chains of conidia; Alternaria produces muriform conidia in chains; Septoria produces elongated pycnidiospores — none match this image.
